findings.title: README's "Managed headers" rule (first-line header, one exception) is false for SKILL.md.tmpl
locations: templates/README.md:26-30 — "A G file carries a first-line header where its format allows a comment... One exception: `queue-guard.sh.tmpl` is copied byte-for-byte... and carries no header"
templates/SKILL.md.tmpl:1-6 — the `<!-- gbg:managed SKILL.md.tmpl ... -->` header sits on line 6, after the five-line YAML frontmatter (`---`/name/description/allowed-tools/`---`), not on line 1
findings.description: The README states the managed-header rule as universal for every G file except one (queue-guard.sh.tmpl, which carries no header at all): 'A G file carries a first-line header where its format allows a comment... One exception: queue-guard.sh.tmpl... carries no header.' But SKILL.md.tmpl — also class G per the same table — does carry the standard Markdown gbg:managed header, just not on the first line: it necessarily follows the YAML frontmatter block (lines 1-5) so the file still parses as a valid Claude Skill. This is a second, undocumented exception to the 'first-line' claim; a reader trusting the README's 'first-line, one exception' statement would misdescribe or mis-implement a check against SKILL.md.tmpl.
findings.resolution_hint: Reword the "Managed headers" paragraph to state two exceptions: queue-guard.sh.tmpl (no header at all) and SKILL.md.tmpl (header present but placed after the mandatory YAML frontmatter, not on line 1).
